# Question (#111)
When and how should an agent-run repository step back and re-architect itself so it keeps every feature and its
robustness at a fraction of the code (owner's example: 100k LOC that could be 20k), without deleting progress?

Scope: triggers (size, churn, duplication, time, merged-PR count), techniques (expert guidance and when each applies),
safe-refactor protocols (feature inventory, characterisation tests, strangler fig), evidence on AI-generated code
growth, existing tools/plugins/skills/repos to reuse, and data from the sibling repos
the four sibling repositories (repo-L, repo-E, repo-R, H) (owner calls them good/bad examples).
Out of scope: language-specific style rules.

Decision it serves: the shape and trigger of an agent-harness component (#113): agent, skill, `uv run dev` command,
plugin, or a mix; Python-first but generic.

Discovery: `uv run dev lit status` on 2026-10-12: OK, partial (s2 down; openalex, crossref, europepmc, arxiv answered).

# Question (#149)
Why do agents in a harness-run repository file a follow-up issue for work they could finish in the same change,
and what rule makes them fix it now without breaking scope discipline?

Scope: how often it happens and what the deferred work cost when it was finally done (agent-filed issues later
closed by a small diff), which harness instructions push towards filing (Owns, one issue per PR, round mode,
hand-back limits, "file the rest", the lead never builds), literature and prior art (self-admitted technical
debt and TODO survival, boy-scout rule, agent scope behaviour and over-caution), and a decision rule.
Data: this machine's Claude Code transcripts and the four sibling repositories (code names repo-L, repo-R,
repo-E, H; mapping in the gitignored .scratch/repos.md). Public repo: code names only, tests/test_scrub.py must pass.

Example (BELIEVED, lead): in one 2026-10-12/13 session on H, workers filed about 25 follow-ups; some were a few
lines inside or next to the issue's Owns (an xfail_strict flag and floor raise, a guard rule, an agent listing).

Decision it serves: the wording of builder, tester, researcher and lead instructions and any gate or hand-back check.

# Question (#169)

How should agents in a harness-run repository find the best existing free software (GitHub repos, PyPI and other
registry packages) before building, including from a section of code, with semantic rather than keyword-only search?
And which agent surface (CLI command, skill, MCP server, subagent, plugin) should carry library discovery, the
literature search (`dev lit`) and the research loop?

Scope: free and keyless (or free-key) sources; Python first, other ecosystems where cheap. Out of scope: paid
services, private registries.

Decision it serves: the defaults of `dev reuse` (#29: sources, query expansion, re-rank, maintenance score,
hallucination guard, `--from` code mode) and whether to add or change skills, agents or MCP servers.

Pilot: [scripts/pilot_recall_bench.py](scripts/pilot_recall_bench.py) (lead, 2026-10-13; results in issue #169).

# Question (#112)
How should an agent-run repository design and maintain its test suite as it grows from small to large: which kinds of
tests, how many, which end-to-end tests are necessary, and how CI/CD should run them?

Scope: test shapes (pyramid, trophy, honeycomb, Google test sizes), empirical data on test counts and test-to-code
ratios, effectiveness measures (coverage vs mutation score), property-based and contract tests, flaky tests, test
selection and impact analysis, CI/CD practice (DORA, stages, merge queues, run time budgets), tests written by LLM
agents (quality, redundancy, gaming), existing tools/plugins/skills to reuse, and data from the sibling repos
the four sibling repositories (repo-L, repo-E, repo-R, H). Extends docs/research/test-floors-and-coverage.md.

Decision it serves: the shape and trigger of an agent-harness test-suite review component (#114) and size-tiered
defaults for the gate and template.

Discovery: `uv run dev lit status` on 2026-10-12: OK, partial (s2 down; openalex, crossref, europepmc, arxiv answered).
